title: I spent the last 6 months of unemployment perfecting my AI trading platform. I'm letting Reddit use it for free.
author: NextgenAITrading
selftext:
I'm a software engineer, and I've spent the past 6 months of unemployment building autonomous AI trading agents. I've gotten it into a state where I'm so confident, that I'm [risking over $40,000 of my real money](https://nexustrade.io/blog/series/public-portfolio-challenge). Despite my confidence, I'm still struggling with top-of-funnel marketing. I have users that LOVE the app, but they're few and far in between. So I decided to do something radical... give away my platform for free.

For the entire month of October, I'm letting users use my platform for absolutely risk free. You can connect to the [MCP server](https://nexustrade.io/ai-trading/claude-ai), backtest a strategy [using the SDK](https://nexustrade.io/developers/python/backtest-a-portfolio), or use the [no-code UI to a perform walk-forward optimization.](https://nexustrade.io/research/methodology/walk-forward-optimization) While I'd very much appreciate feedback in exchange for this offer, it's not required. Just claim it, cancel if you want to (while maintaining your benefits) and try to see if you can build your own AI trading agent.

[Claim your 3 free months!](https://nexustrade.io/october?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=paid_social&utm_campaign=october-free-2026&utm_content=ad-01)

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: For the MCP server, what prevents an agent from moving a strategy from research into live execution with broader permissions than the user intended? I’d want separate paper/live tool scopes, per-order and portfolio notional limits, an immutable approval log, and a kill switch. It would also help if an SDK backtest and the no-code walk-forward optimizer exported the same strategy specification, so users can reproduce one path in the other. The $40,000 personal allocation shows commitment, but not validation; the attached image is biographical and displays no legible performance statistics.

replies.author: NextgenAITrading
replies.body:
This is an excellent question and I'm glad you asked!

Paper-trading is always fully autonomous. Live-trading is semi-autonomous unless you get explicit approval. The agent is physically unable to send live orders to your brokerage without your permission. There are also portfolio events, so you know **exactly** the specific conditions of your strategy that caused an order to be staged. Finally, if you are approved, you can configure the number of orders per day that are executed autonomously. 

>It would also help if an SDK backtest and the no-code walk-forward optimizer exported the same strategy specification, so users can reproduce one path in the other

Already done!
